_comment: Frozen column contracts. A column name here is a promise: renaming or reordering one breaks every file and every reader that already uses it. Change these only by adding a new version, never by editing in place. See Guide_To_Column_Contracts.md.

model_eval_ledger._note: Added v16 (2026-08-25) alongside keep_the_model_eval_ledger.py - the ledger the Model_Eval_Runner appends real evaluation results to (W4.1 schema; W4.2 writes ROWS only, never this contract). One row per (suite, task, model) run: score/max_score, seed and temperature so a run can be reproduced, tokens/duration so its cost is visible, machine so nobody mistakes a GPU number for a laptop one, notes for honest labelling, version for the envelope convention. Append-only: corrections are new rows with the same key shape and a later run_ts - never an overwrite. An untested model shows NO rows; 'untested' is rendered honestly on the grid, never guessed.

equity_price_ledger._note: Added v15 (2026-08-25) alongside append_the_price_ledger.py - the contract the module promised in its docstring before any column existed. One row per held exchange-traded symbol per day. v15 also carries the FIRST event envelope (see Guide_To_The_Trace_Ledger.md): every row written since has event_id (UUID), written_at (IST instant), version (envelope version 1) and supersedes (the event_id this row corrects - empty for a first observation). Corrections are NEW rows that supersede; nothing is ever overwritten, so pre-envelope six-column rows remain valid history and are all still 'current'. Readers that want today's truth use current_rows(), which drops rows another row's supersedes points at.

fund_analysis_ledger._note: Added v13 (2026-08-22) alongside analyse_a_fund.py. One row per fund per day: the holdings-analysis numbers behind each fund's button on the Investments tab - splits, market-cap buckets, top sector, weighted P/E / P/B and the advanced ratios. Same-day re-runs replace that day's row; history across days is kept so a portfolio review can watch a fund drift. Company facts come from Yahoo via yfinance; sector coverage depends on the unverified hand map, which classified_coverage_pct admits.

fund_nav_ledger._note: Added v12 (2026-08-22) alongside track_the_nav_ledger.py. One row per fund per refresh: the NAV mfapi.in published, when it published it, and when INKY wrote it down. Re-running on the same day replaces that day's row; history across days is kept so staleness has a file behind it. The Investments tab's freshness badge reads this.

portfolio_holdings._note: Was frozen with owner 'market' and no file, for a screen that was never built separately. Finance absorbed the Investments concept instead (see Start_Here_Main_Guide.md) - owner and path updated 2026-08-16, columns unchanged since the contract was never touched by a reader. read_portfolio_holdings.py is the only writer; scheme_name and amfi_code are never editable from the UI, since changing either would silently turn one holding into a different one.

active_sips._note: Recurring monthly SIP amounts, one row per fund. Informational - never added into the surplus formula automatically, same rule as assets_and_liabilities.

realized_capital_gains._note: One row per matched buy/sell pair from a capital-gains report, written once by import_from_broker_statements.py. Deliberately has no folio_number column - C2, that is exactly the kind of identifier .gitignore's raw-statement rule exists to keep out of a tracked file.

job_applications._note: Contract frozen. No file yet - this screen is not built.

notable_expenses._note: Manual entry only. Big or recurring items. Not a daily expense log — everything else stays inside slice_usage_actual.

model_call_log._note: One row per model call. Written by the router when it is built. Every number on the Models screen is counted from this file - nothing is stored twice. 'check_results' used to be called 'gate_results', which collided with Finance's four investment gates; renamed in ADR-044 while the file was still empty.

free_tier_ledger._note: One row per attempt against a free allowance, written by keep_the_free_tier_ledger.py. Counts what has already been used so a scheduled job never discovers a limit by hitting it.

assets_and_liabilities._note: Hand-typed. What I own and what I owe, outside the surplus formula - track_assets_and_liabilities.py never feeds this back into the noticeboard automatically, so nothing is counted twice.

my_investments._note: Hand-typed, one row per transaction, never per holding. A correction is a new row, so the history survives. read_what_i_own.py derives every holding from this file.

resource_guardian_actions._note: One row per process the_resource_guardian.py ever actually ends - append-only, so a morning read of what happened overnight is a file, not a guess. Only ever a process named in resource_guardian_kill_list.json, which a person writes in advance.

needs_human._note: Where the router and the agent supervisor both escalate - one file, one schema, so a person has one place to look. A model may never write or clear this file - only do_one_task.escalate_to_human() appends, and only a person clears it.

study_sessions._note: One row per completed study block, written by track_study_sessions.py when a block is stopped, never on start. A block abandoned without stopping leaves no row - an unfinished session is not a lie half-told, it is simply not recorded yet. `capture` was appended as the LAST column at v14 (the work-capture line: what day-job work taught or produced today); rows written before v14 read as an empty capture cell, never a missing column.

recall_reviews._note: One row per time a Knowledge_Base note was marked reviewed, written by manage_recall_schedule.py. box_after is the Leitner box the note moved to - never edited by hand, always the result of the review just recorded.

waiting_for_you._note: The reversibility gate (Shared_By_All_Agents/the_reversibility_gate.py). An agent stops here before anything irreversible and waits for approve/refuse - never a third state.
